NDT Level III consulting for Hawaii: what can be done remotely and what needs a visit

For Hawaii inspection companies and asset owners, most NDT Level III work can be done remotely: written practices, procedures, technique sheets, certification records and audit preparation. Atlantis provides that as an outsourced ASNT NDT Level III service, schedules on-island visits after a scoping call, and keeps the scope plain: it is not an Authorized Inspection Agency and never signs as inspector of record.

Work that travels well. A written practice can be drafted or revised against SNT-TC-1A, reviewed with the company's managers on video and issued for signature without anyone flying. The same applies to method procedures and technique sheets, review of certification files for missing vision examinations or undocumented experience hours, review of inspection reports and data, and a mock client audit run against the company's own records. Outsourced ASNT Level III services, procedure development and SNT-TC-1A programme set-up describe each of these.

Work that needs a visit or a shipment. Practical examinations need specimens with known discontinuities, and those either travel with the examiner or are shipped ahead, which takes planning from the mainland. Reference blocks and calibration standards are in the same position, as is instrument calibration that has to be done off-island. Theory training can run online through NDT training in Hawaii, with practice on the Practical NDT simulator, so an on-island visit can concentrate on practical examinations.

Hawaii's regulators. The National Board lists the Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, through its Division of Occupational Safety and Health's Boiler and Elevator Inspection Branch, as Hawaii's boiler and pressure vessel jurisdiction. Hawaii is not an NRC Agreement State, so the NRC itself, through its Region IV office, licenses radioactive materials used for industrial radiography there. The NRC's industrial radiography rules in 10 CFR Part 34 carry their own radiographer certification requirement, separate from the employer's SNT-TC-1A certification, and a Hawaii radiography company's written practice has to sit alongside its NRC licence conditions without contradicting them. Consulting covers the NDT side; radiation safety officer duties stay with the licensee.

Practical points for planning Hawaii engagements:

  • Hawaii does not observe daylight saving time, so the gap to the mainland changes twice a year and meeting times should be fixed in Hawaii time.
  • Small island inspection companies often need a named Level III for audits rather than a full-time hire, which is the gap an outsourced service fills.
  • Federal and defence work follows the contracting agency's own NDT personnel requirements, which are checked before any commitment is made.

Certification records, instrument calibration and procedure revisions can be kept in Atlantis ERP certificate tracking, so an auditor can see which revision and which certification applied on a given date. To start a Hawaii engagement, request a scoping call.
